failureClass: A container's status marker or unregistered restatement silently promotes a weaker claim.
method: Fresh coverage audit rather than checking Agent 3's six repairs: (1) count status-bearing prose against registered claim identities; (2) trace every live register claim to home/restatement enforcement; (3) inspect summaries and artifact indexes for stale or unmarked candidate claims; (4) inspect the checker's predicates and mutation self-tests to identify false-negative classes.

resolves.A2-C3-RV-01: BLOCKER: claim-register.v1.json has 10 claims while architecture/ and steering/ contain 81 explicit SEALED/CANDIDATE/REOPENED/OPEN markers and numerous named decisions such as D3, P-1..P-3, and extension/capability decisions. Marker count is not a claim count, but the concrete omissions disprove 'every decision exactly one ID'.
resolves.A2-C3-RV-02: BLOCKER: no current claim has a _probe. CHK-1 therefore skips location-level status checking for all registered claims and cannot enforce its advertised no-promotion property.
resolves.A2-C3-RV-03: BLOCKER: CHK-3 contains hand-written signatures for only three claims and --self-test mutates only CHK-1, CHK-2, and CHK-4. The worked statement that all recurrences are reproduced is not supported.
resolves.A2-C3-RV-04: BLOCKER: C-2 is CANDIDATE in its home/register but architecture/00 line 118 and architecture/11 line 82 restate 'one mechanism, typed logical stages' without an inline C-2 candidate marker. check-claims.py passes: an observed false negative of the exact recurrence class.
resolves.A2-C3-RV-05: BLOCKER: architecture/11 lines 67-70 says C-1 remains candidate and P-4 is open, despite the register sealing both. Its artifact table still points to D9 v1.2 and R-1 v1 after v1.3/v1.1 were authored.
resolves.A2-C3-RV-06: BLOCKER: architecture/07 and architecture/09 still describe D9 v1.1/v1.2 as current while the register binds v1.3. A single-source claim that readers must mentally override is not mechanically enforced purity.
resolves.A2-C3-RV-07: BLOCKER: architecture/05 still calls the rejected global ordering a 'semantics-first correction'. That wording can reintroduce the C-1 overcorrection even though C-1's home is now correct.

sealedPropertiesCovered.property: Every decision claim has one authoritative status, and no home, restatement, summary, or container presents a stronger status.
Candidate claims cannot be used as settled premises through an unmarked summary.
The repair author's checker is challenged by coverage and mutation analysis rather than merely re-run as corroboration.

falsifiableEvidence.observedFalseNegative: With C-2 CANDIDATE, the unmarked architecture/00 and architecture/11 restatements still pass python3 artifacts/check-claims.py.

independentVerdict.agent3SixRepairs: Several instance repairs hold, but they do not establish the failure-class invariant.
independentVerdict.claimRegisterMechanism: CANDIDATE with named blockers, not a proven enforcement mechanism
independentVerdict.confidence: high because the current checker passes a concrete stronger-than-register restatement

requiredSuccessorArtifact.name: claim-register.v2.json + checker conformance suite
requirements: Inventory every named decision claim, including open and candidate claims, with stable IDs and machine-resolvable home/restatement locations.
Reject a restatement of a candidate/reopened/open claim that lacks an equal-or-weaker inline status, including summary tables and headings.
Reject missing or stale binding-artifact references and contradictory version/status prose.
Generate claim signatures or require explicit claim IDs in prose; do not depend on three hand-written phrases.
Mutation-test every checker invariant, including CHK-3, unregistered claims, stale artifact bindings, and articulation-reference reclassification.
Make the checker fail on the currently observed unmarked C-2 restatements before repairing the prose.

whatWouldChangeMyMind: A successor checker that first fails on the current C-2 and stale-index cases, then passes only after complete register coverage and document repairs, with mutation tests for every enforcement rule.
knownLimitations: The 81-marker count includes container statuses and is not asserted to equal the number of claims; the verdict relies on specific omitted decisions and a demonstrated C-2 false negative.
This audit does not claim every stale sentence has been enumerated; the checker must make that enumeration mechanical.
The static-analysis MCP remains bound to the wrong project root, so no MCP graph evidence was used and refresh_graph was not called.
